decisions.settledAnswer: The implementation makes each of the five reads of the live service, and the maintainer makes none. A read is a look that changes nothing: no row, no check, and no pull request. Reads 1 to 3 are 3 wrangler commands from a fixed list: the place of the production database, 5 row counts, and the list of the databases of the account. Each statement is a SELECT, and nothing else runs. The implementation checks in each result that rows_written is 0 and that changed_db is false, and it writes each result in the issue that uses it. Reads 4 and 5 are two pages of the Cloudflare dashboard, which the implementation opens in the Chrome session of the maintainer: the CPU time of one run page in the traces of the Worker visonaut, and the request count of the Worker visonaut-compare. The implementation reads the two numbers there, and each result is in the record. It reads the request count before the last step of D-CODE-02 deletes the Worker, and it reads the CPU time before the change of D-RUN-03 is live.
decisions.forImplementation: The placement key of the issue tooling and steps 2 and 3 of the issue compare-worker no longer wait for the maintainer: the implementation runs the 3 commands and reads the 2 dashboard pages, after it tests that the wrangler login is valid.

decisions.settledAnswer: The public repository gets the steps to use the 7 findings only after their fix is in production. The 7 findings are TRUST-01, AUTH-09, AUTH-16, AUTH-07, TRUST-10, AUTH-14, and TRUST-02. Until then, the issues and the pull requests of these findings have the short form: they name the change, its file, and its lines, and they leave out the steps, the chain, and the cost numbers. Each other issue has the full detail from the start. The lab goes to the branch when the audit ends, without the folder apps/lab/audit. That folder is added to the branch after two things: the fixes of the 7 findings are in production, and the one UPDATE of D-AUTH-05 ran. A comment on each of these issues then links to the record. The contract pull request with the row that names what one of these fixes repairs opens only after the first of these fixes is deployed.
decisions.forImplementation: The issue set can be filed now with the issue access in its short form, the private briefs stay off GitHub, and the lab branch is first pushed without apps/lab/audit.

decisions.settledAnswer: The log of a background pass can say why a pass failed, with three fixed values. Each place that catches an error in a pass can log the name of the error class (for example SecurityError or ConflictError), the fixed code of a SecurityError (for example github_unavailable), and the HTTP status number that GitHub answered. Each value is on a list in the source code, and a name that is not on the list becomes "other". The log never gets a message text or a stack. No D1 write is added.
decisions.forImplementation: The issue ops adds about 20 lines (estimate) that log errorName, code, and upstreamStatus from fixed lists, with the change of row 7 or in one more pull request.

decisions.settledAnswer: For a GitHub webhook that starts no work, the service writes nothing to D1. One new function says, before the service writes, if a webhook can start work. For a webhook with no work, the service checks the signature and the repository, writes one log line, and answers 202. A webhook with work is saved as today, with its receipt in the table github_webhook_delivery. No receipt that exists is deleted.
decisions.forImplementation: The issue ops gets one more pull request: a tested function that sorts the webhooks before the receipt, with no migration.

decisions.settledAnswer: When Submit fails because of one screenshot file, the message of the CLI names that screenshot in the CI log. A message about a file that the CLI cannot read or accept has the item key, the variant key, and the two numbers, for example: "dialog/open (react-light): 1248x1700 is 2,121,600 pixels. The limit is 2,100,000." The CLI prints the two keys only. It does not print the display title of a test, and it never prints a result of the comparison (changed, approved, or rejected). The public check gets no screenshot name, as D-OPS-07 says.
decisions.forImplementation: The issue cli gets one more pull request (about 30 lines in 3 files, estimate), which must be merged before the one CLI release of the cutover.

decisions.settledAnswer: The service does not check the screenshot files itself before it stores them, and nothing is built. The service keeps its two checks of today: it compares the number of bytes and the SHA-256 digest of each uploaded image with the list that the Submit job sent. It does not open the file. The CLI in the Submit job is the program that checks each image. The contract says this in plain words: the CLI in the Submit job checks each image, and the service checks only the size and the digest.
decisions.forImplementation: No code is added: the sentence of the contract row for D-CODE-02 stays as drafted, the last step of the issue compare-worker can go, and the new review page must keep the load, decode, and size checks before Approve.

decisions.settledAnswer: The new issues get priority and difficulty labels. The repository ariakit/visonaut gets the labels p0, p1, p2, easy, and hard, with the names, the descriptions, and the colors of ariakit/ariakit. The account of the maintainer creates them one time. The ariakit-bot identity then puts one priority label on each issue, and easy or hard when it applies. The note of the maintainer adds four permissions. The existing labels of the repository can be removed. The relevant labels of ariakit/ariakit, which are the ones that make sense for this project, are copied with their colors. A new label can be created where it makes sense. No further question to the maintainer is necessary for these label changes. This answer does not select the label set beyond the 5 labels: the work that prepares the filing of the issues selects it.
decisions.forImplementation: Before the filing, the label set is selected and created (the 9 default labels can go), and each issue then gets one priority label, and easy or hard where it applies, with the ariakit-bot identity.

decisions.settledAnswer: The contract approves the settled design with its own text. A contract pull request replaces each changed UI rule with its new text: the variant control, the place of Approve and Reject, the list and its filter, the row picture, the zoom levels, the result page, and the header. The contract then stands alone: a reader needs no tag and no file of the lab. The lab is an example and not a source of rules. The answer does not open the design again.
